subject: deepagents
title: LLM classifier batch-reviews tool calls behind deterministic allow/deny, failing to a human on unavailability with a latched bad spec
one_why: Approvals get a second, model-agnostic adjudicator between 'policy allows' and 'ask the human', and every failure mode (classifier down, bad model spec, repeated denials, oversized context) is engineered to fail toward a human, not toward auto-approve - distinct from codex's guardian-reviewer-pool which reviews actions in-process rather than as a batched classifier with escalation counters; tests assert the fail-closed branches (test_auto_mode.py:742,2339,3012).

subject: deepagents
title: DeltaChannel messages reducer with periodic snapshots cuts LangGraph checkpoint growth from O(N^2) to O(N)
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/graph.py:74-77 (DeltaChannel(_messages_delta_reducer, snapshot_frequency=50)); libs/deepagents/deepagents/_messages_reducer.py:31-60 (dedup by id, RemoveMessage tombstones, id assignment deliberately deferred to LangGraph replay hook)
one_why: Long-horizon agents rewrite the whole message list into every checkpoint superlinearly; the reducer's fast-path skips convert_to_messages on already-typed state and refuses to assign ids because 'a reducer runs on replay too, where a randomly-assigned ID would differ from the one stored in the checkpoint' - a replay-determinism insight most session-journal designs miss.

subject: deepagents
title: Filesystem permissions enforced per-tool with conservative recursive-delete semantics, and construction fails closed when paired with an execute-capable backend
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/filesystem.py:502-587 (deny blocks ancestor/wildcard-overlapping delete), :1792-1801 (NotImplementedError on permissions+SandboxBackendProtocol); middleware/_fs_interrupt.py:24-46 (pathless bulk grep fires unconditionally for any interrupt rule)
one_why: Two honesty moves over the standard tested-approval 6-rung: a deny pattern anywhere in the ancestor chain blocks a recursive delete even when the leaf is unlisted, and the permissions story does NOT silently claim to cover `execute` - it refuses to build rather than ship a policy the shell tool bypasses. Gap is real and documented: permissions bind at the tool layer only, not on direct backend use (graph.py:454-457).

subject: deepagents
title: Three tiers (tool-arg truncation -> fraction-triggered summarization -> provider-overflow recovery with one budgeted retry) plus reversible backend offload
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/summarization.py:171-196 (TruncateArgsSettings), :257-286 (model-profile-driven fraction vs conservative fixed defaults), :1542-1548 (context-overflow catch -> summarize+clip, exactly one retry, else ContextOverflowError), :1571-1580 (offload to backend BEFORE summarizing so eviction is reversible)
one_why: Falls short of codex's no-LLM fresh-window tier (9) but adds two things the corpus rarely pairs: eviction writes full history to /conversation_history before summarizing (data-loss is warned, not silent), and a provider-overflow error triggers a bounded recovery ladder instead of a hard cap dumped on the human - the anti-pattern codel demonstrates. Trigger defaults switch to fraction-based only when the model profile advertises max_input_tokens.

subject: deepagents
title: Middleware stack ordered so memory writes never invalidate the Anthropic cache prefix, and assembled system prompt pinned by golden snapshot tests
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/graph.py:904-905 ('memory updates ... don't invalidate the Anthropic prompt cache prefix'), :380-383 (SystemMessage cache_control markers preserved through assembly), :843-960 (cache middleware before Memory in tail order); tests/unit_tests/test_graph.py:723; tests/unit_tests/smoke_tests/test_system_prompt.py
one_why: Cache discipline is encoded in assembly ordering rather than runtime: profile middleware is placed before Memory specifically so the mutable system-prompt segment sits after the cache breakpoint, and the exact assembled prompt is frozen by snapshot tests so a middleware-ordering regression fails CI - distinct from pi's active warming and smelt's fuzzed-prefix invariant.

subject: deepagents
title: Fake chat models drive the real create_deep_agent graph end-to-end, including the async-subagent round-trip against a mocked LangGraph SDK
evidence: libs/deepagents/tests/unit_tests/chat_model.py:21-50 (GenericFakeChatModel with configurable stream chunking + call recording); tests/unit_tests/test_end_to_end.py:3441-3500 (asserts async_tasks state transition through a real agent.invoke)
one_why: Tests exercise the actual middleware stack and graph, not a mock harness - the async-subagent e2e asserts the full model-emits-tool-call -> mocked-remote-exec -> state-updated -> model-responds cycle, which is what makes 250k Python test LOC (census-corrected) load-bearing rather than existence-assertions; no live provider key needed.

subject: deepagents
title: Rubric middleware gates completion: a separate grader sub-agent re-enters the loop with feedback until satisfied/failed/max_iterations
one_why: Convergence with codex-infinity's arc-monitor and smelt's goal-gated continue: completion is decided by an independent grader against a declared rubric, not by 'model stopped emitting tool calls' - here implemented as reusable middleware rather than a bespoke outer loop.

subject: deepagents
title: test_loc inflated ~45% by vendored JSON datasets sitting under directories named tests
evidence: libs/evals/tests/evals/tau2_airline/data/db.json (205,192 LOC), tasks.json (3,521), libs/evals/tests/evals/data/benchmark_samples/bfcl_v3_final.json (1,533); cloc over all dirs named 'tests' sums to exactly 471,723 = census test_loc
one_why: Census-discipline finding: the 'tests>prod' signal is real (~257k py/js test logic vs ~172k non-test Python code LOC) but the 471k headline is 45% fixture data; any glob that treats a tests/-named path as test code will mis-rank eval-heavy repos - synthesis should subtract JSON data blobs from test LOC before comparing test-to-prod ratios.

subject: deepagents
title: Two commit-pinned auto-generated THREAT_MODEL docs (SDK + CLI) stating scope, out-of-scope, and blunt assumptions
evidence: libs/deepagents/THREAT_MODEL.md:1-60 ('does not provide OS-level process isolation' assumption 5; OpenAI Responses-API data-retention caveat assumption 8); libs/code/THREAT_MODEL.md:1-3 ('Generated: 2026-08-19')
one_why: Same honesty register as pi's SECURITY.md and smelt's trust model, but mechanized: pinned to a commit hash and regenerated, so the doc can be diffed against code drift - a template worth copying for keeping posture docs from rotting, and the assumptions double as the license/isolation boundary the rubric rewards.

subject: deepagents
title: Sophisticated model-eval infra wired only to workflow_dispatch, never to a PR or cron trigger
evidence: .github/workflows/evals.yml:36 (on: workflow_dispatch only), unified_evals.yml:19-30 (branch-compare + frozen lite task sets), evals_trials.yml (N-trial 6h-budget aggregation); nightly cron _benchmark_nightly.yml:8-10 runs CodSpeed PERF only
one_why: This is the specific reason verification caps at 8 despite a best-in-class eval harness (per-provider matrices, N-trial aggregation, branch A/B): the quality signal exists but is opt-in, so no PR is ever blocked by a model-quality regression - contrast ci.yml which does gate lint/unit on every PR, even fail-closing the warnings-bypass when the labels API errors (_test.yml:135).
